paragraphs.title: The Departure of the Righteous and Rebuke of Idolaters

answers: They are taken away from the evil to come
easy.explanation: The verse says that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.
easy.q: What happens to the righteous in verse 1?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, "He shall enter into peace."
easy.q: What will the righteous enter after death?

easy.explanation: The prophet addresses "ye sons of the sorceress."
easy.q: To whom does the prophet call, "Draw near hither"?

answers: They do not consider the meaning of his removal
medium.explanation: The verse says, "no man layeth it to heart" and "none considering."
medium.q: What does the people's lack of concern for the righteous show?

medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the people as a generation marked by falsehood.
medium.q: What does the phrase "a seed of falsehood" describe?

answers: Under green trees, in valleys, and among rocks
medium.explanation: The passage mentions green trees, valleys, cliffs of rocks, and high mountains.
medium.q: Where is idolatrous worship described in these verses?

answers: The righteous enter peace, while the idolaters are rebuked
The righteous worship idols, while the idolaters rest
There is no contrast in the passage
challenge.explanation: The righteous are described as entering peace, while the idolaters receive prophetic condemnation.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the righteous and the idolaters in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The question expresses God's rejection of the practices described.
challenge.q: What does the question "Should I receive comfort in these?" communicate?

answers: The nation's relationships and forbidden practices had expanded
A resting place was built for the righteous
challenge.explanation: The expression belongs to the description of unfaithfulness and covenants with others.
challenge.q: What does "thou hast enlarged thy bed" mean in context?

paragraphs.title: Turning Away from God and Making Covenants with Strangers

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that she debased herself "even unto hell."
easy.q: Where did the woman go after debasing herself?

easy.explanation: She had not remembered God or laid Him to her heart.

answers: The one who trusts in God
The one who boasts in himself
easy.explanation: The verse says, "he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land."

answers: She became weary but did not say there was no hope
medium.explanation: The verse says, "Thou art wearied in the greatness of thy way; yet saidst thou not, There is no hope."
medium.q: What was the result of her many efforts and journeys?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to losing hope, though she did not say it.
medium.q: What does "There is no hope" mean in this context?

answers: The companies are carried away by the wind, but the trusting person inherits the land
The companies rest, while the trusting person wanders
The companies are faithful, while the trusting person is forgotten
medium.explanation: The wind carries the companies away, but the one who trusts in God receives an inheritance.
medium.q: What is the contrast between her companies and the person who trusts in God?

answers: External effort does not guarantee fellowship with God
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts exhausting activity and forgetfulness with trusting God.
challenge.q: What does forgetting God while pursuing many efforts teach?

answers: The wind will give them an inheritance
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes their weakness and passing nature.
challenge.q: What does "the wind shall carry them all away" suggest about the companies?

answers: As a pursuit that accompanies spiritual unfaithfulness
As a source of immediate healing
As a relationship belonging only to the righteous
challenge.explanation: The passage connects foreign alliances and efforts with forgetting God and spiritual departure.
challenge.q: How is the nation's relationship with foreign powers portrayed?

paragraphs.title: Clearing the Way and Comforting the Humble

easy.explanation: The command is, "Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way."
easy.q: What are the people commanded to do to the way?

answers: With the contrite and humble in spirit
easy.explanation: God says that He dwells with the contrite and humble in spirit.
easy.q: With whom does the high and lofty One dwell?

answers: He revives their spirit and heart
He hides them from the way
easy.explanation: The verse says He will revive the spirit of the humble and the heart of the contrite.
easy.q: What does God do for the humble and contrite?

answers: To prepare the way of God's people
To lead the people away from light
To build places of idolatrous worship
medium.explanation: The command concerns preparing the way and removing obstacles from the path of God's people.
medium.q: Why is the stumblingblock removed from the way?

medium.explanation: A contrite person is humble, brokenhearted, and repentant.
medium.q: What does "contrite" mean in this passage?

answers: He has made the spirits and souls and does not wish them to fail
medium.explanation: God says He will not be angry forever because the spirit and souls are His creation.
medium.q: Why will God not contend for ever?

answers: Although He is exalted, He revives the brokenhearted
His greatness prevents Him from seeing them
He dwells only in the highest place
challenge.explanation: The passage presents God as high and holy while also dwelling with the humble.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God's greatness and His nearness to the humble?

answers: A road that can never be opened
challenge.explanation: The repetition strengthens the command to prepare the way and remove obstacles.
challenge.q: What does the repeated command "Cast ye up, cast ye up" emphasize?

answers: From brokenness to renewed life and strength
challenge.explanation: God promises to revive their spirit and heart.
challenge.q: What change is described for the humble and contrite?

easy.explanation: Verse 17 refers to "the iniquity of his covetousness."
easy.q: For what sin was God angry and smote the sinner?

answers: He sent him back to the sea
easy.explanation: God says, "I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also."
easy.q: What did God do after seeing the sinner's ways?

answers: To him that is far off and to him that is near
To the king and his princes
To the sea and the land
easy.explanation: The verse says, "Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near."

answers: Sin and punishment, then healing, guidance, and comfort
medium.explanation: The passage moves from anger and hiding to healing, leading, restoration, and peace.
medium.q: What sequence is described in this passage?

answers: Words or praise spoken by the lips
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to what the lips produce, especially the proclamation of peace.
medium.q: What does "the fruit of the lips" refer to in this context?

answers: Because of the sinner's iniquity and his froward way
Because the people were already healed
Because the road had been cleared
medium.explanation: God's hiding is described in connection with covetousness and walking in the way of the heart.
medium.q: Why did God hide His face before the healing?

answers: Punishment does not exclude the possibility of correction and mercy
Sin is not important at all
Healing comes only after eternal punishment
challenge.explanation: God rebukes sin but also sees, heals, leads, and restores the sinner.
challenge.q: What does the movement from punishment to healing teach about God's response to sinners?

answers: The fullness and certainty of the peace proclaimed
A difference between the far and the near
challenge.explanation: The repetition intensifies the announcement of peace and healing.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated words "Peace, peace"?

answers: God sees the person's ways and chooses to heal and guide him
God cannot see the ways and therefore punishes him
The ways prevent any possibility of healing
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects seeing the ways with healing and leading.
challenge.q: How are healing and comfort connected to seeing a person's ways?

paragraphs.title: The Turmoil of the Wicked and the Absence of Peace

easy.explanation: The passage says, "the wicked are like the troubled sea."
easy.q: To what are the wicked compared?

easy.explanation: The sea is described as one "that cannot rest."
easy.q: What can the troubled sea not do?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, "There is no peace ... to the wicked."
easy.q: What do the wicked not have?

medium.explanation: The verse says that its waters cast up "mire and dirt."
medium.q: What do the waters of the troubled sea cast up?

medium.explanation: Mire is mud or foul, dirty matter.
medium.q: What does "mire" mean in the phrase "mire and dirt"?

answers: They are in turmoil and cannot become still
medium.explanation: The restless sea represents the inner unrest of the wicked.
medium.q: Why is there no peace for the wicked according to the image of the sea?

answers: Both portray inner turmoil and a lack of rest
There is no connection between the image and the wicked
challenge.explanation: The troubled sea serves as a picture of the wicked person's unrest.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the troubled sea and the wicked?

answers: It emphasizes the harmful and defiling results of their turmoil
It presents them as a source of purity
challenge.explanation: Mire and dirt portray the damaging and defiling results cast up by the troubled sea.
challenge.q: What does the image of mire and dirt add to the description of the wicked?

answers: Peace is offered to those who turn to God, but the wicked have no peace
Even the righteous are denied peace
Peace is described only as a natural phenomenon
challenge.explanation: Earlier, peace is proclaimed to those who are far and near; the chapter ends by denying peace to the wicked.
challenge.q: How does the ending of the chapter relate to the earlier promise of peace?
